system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent AbbVie Biotechnology Ltd; counterparty is Harpoon Therapeutics, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

input.quote: 10.2 Additional Representations and Warranties of Harpoon. Except as set forth on Schedule 10.2, Harpoon further represents and warrants to AbbVie, as of the Effective Date, as follows:
input.rationale: Article 10 contains only mutual and Harpoon-specific representations given "as of the Effective Date" (10.1, 10.2) plus covenants (10.3) — there is no forward-looking performance warranty. The closest performance standard, Section 3.8.4 ("in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law"), is a mutual compliance covenant, not a conformance warranty, and carries no warranty remedy. Nothing in the Agreement warrants that Harpoon's deliverables (including the Final Development Report) or any software will conform to their documentation, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy exists anywhere (searches for "conform", "re-perform" and "refund" return only tax and indemnity mechanics, and all payments are expressed as non-refundable). The disclaimer at 10.5 is acceptable because it preserves "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so no carve-out edit is needed — but it leaves nothing to preserve. This fails the fallback on material terms (no conformance warranty, no duration, no remedy), so we inserted the shortest express warranty at fallback level: 90 days for software/deliverables, 30 days for the Initial Development Activities, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund. We did not take the preferred 12-month software period, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code elements, which are not apposite to this development and option agreement.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** WARRANTY — **deviation**, cured at the fallback level with one insertion.

- **What exists:** Article 10 gives only Effective-Date representations (10.1 mutual, 10.2 Harpoon-specific, Schedule-qualified) and covenants (10.3/10.4). Section 3.8.4 requires Development activities "in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law," but that is a mutual compliance covenant, not a conformance warranty, and has no remedy attached.
- **What is absent:** no conformance warranty for Harpoon's deliverables (including the Final Development Report) or any software, no warranty period, and no repair/replacement/refund remedy anywhere in the document.
- **Disclaimer check:** 10.5 opens with "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN," so it does not swallow express warranties — no carve-out edit required, and none was made.
- **Cure:** new Section 10.6 inserted after 10.5, at fallback thresholds only (90 days software/deliverables, 30 days services) with repair, replacement, re-performance or refund. Preferred-only elements (12-month software period, compliance-with-laws, no malicious code) were deliberately not volunteered.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Fallback is position-complete: the inserted "Performance Warranty" supplies a 90-day software/deliverable conformance warranty, a 30-day services (Initial Development Activities) warranty, and repair/replace, re-performance and refund remedies — all four fallback elements are in operative text, not merely promised in the comment.
- Preferred is not met: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty. This is a correct 'deviation' finding pitched at fallback.
- Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise clause, nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, and Section 10.5 is correctly left untouched because it already carves out "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN". No survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure or extra damages categories were added.
- Intent defect to repair: the drafter's own analysis records that payments under this Agreement are expressed as non-refundable. The new remedy "refund the amounts paid for them" therefore sits against a retained contradictory sentence and may be read as inoperative. Repair by opening the remedy sentence with "Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable," (citing the specific payment section).
- Two drafting points the reviewer should expect Harpoon to contest, neither fatal to minimality: (i) remedy choice is placed "at AbbVie's election" whereas the playbook model language puts it at Vendor's option — keep it, but be ready to trade; (ii) "including the Final Development Report" is an illustrative inclusion that is not required by any selected element and can be dropped if it draws fire.
- Optional scope tightening: the services leg is anchored to "Initial Development Activities" only. If Harpoon performs other Development activities or services under the Agreement (e.g. Manufacturing support), consider "the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder" so the warranty is not under-inclusive.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

Resubmitted with the verifier's required repair.

**Changes made to the redline:**

1. **Contradiction removed (mandated repair):** the remedy sentence now opens "Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable, including Sections 6.1 through 6.4, ..." — I re-read Sections 6.1 (upfront, "non-refundable, non-creditable"), 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4 (each "non-refundable" milestone payments) and cited that range so the refund leg cannot be read as inoperative against retained payment language. Those sections themselves are left verbatim, so the unrelated commercial bargain on non-refundability of upfront and milestone consideration is untouched outside the warranty remedy.
2. **Illustrative inclusion dropped:** "including the Final Development Report" removed — it was not required by any selected element and gave Harpoon an easy target.
3. **Services leg de-narrowed:** now "the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder", so the 30-day warranty is not under-inclusive of other Harpoon-performed activities.
4. **Kept as advised:** "at AbbVie's election" retained (flagged as a likely trade, not a defect); Section 10.5 still untouched because it already carves out express warranties; no survival tail, expense allocation, notice procedure or extra damages categories added.

Level remains **fallback** (90 days software/deliverables, 30 days services, repair/replace, re-performance, refund); preferred-only elements were again not volunteered. Minimality validated `ok:true`.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule and exact checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Services are warranted for at least 30 days.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Warranty remedies include a refund.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Article 10 contains only mutual and Harpoon-specific representations given "as of the Effective Date" (10.1, 10.2) plus covenants (10.3, 10.4). The closest performance standard, Section 3.8.4 ("in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law"), is a mutual compliance covenant, not a conformance warranty, and carries no remedy. Nothing warrants that Harpoon's deliverables or any software conform to their documentation, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy exists (searches for "conform", "re-perform" and "refund" return only tax and indemnity mechanics). The disclaimer at 10.5 preserves "THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so it needs no carve-out edit — but there is nothing for it to preserve. This fails the fallback on material terms, so we inserted the shortest express warranty at fallback level: 90 days for software/deliverables, 30 days for Harpoon's Development activities, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund. Because Sections 6.1 through 6.4 make payments "non-refundable", the remedy sentence opens with a narrow override so the refund leg is not read as inoperative; the services leg also reaches Harpoon's other Development activities so the warranty is not under-inclusive. We did not take the preferred 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code elements.

Harpoon warrants that (a) for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation, and (b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner. Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable, including Sections 6.1 through 6.4, for breach of this warranty Harpoon shall, at AbbVie's election, repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, re-perform the non-conforming activities, or refund the amounts paid for them.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] Article 10 gives us only as-of-Effective-Date representations, with no conformance warranty for Harpoon's deliverables or Development activities and no remedy for non-conforming work. We added a short express warranty at our fallback position (90 days for software and other deliverables, 30 days for Harpoon's Development activities) with repair, replacement, re-performance or refund, and we open the remedy with a narrow override so the refund is not defeated by the non-refundable payment language in Sections 6.1 through 6.4.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall ..." — both trigger events, any cause, covered.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted (a) provides assistance "for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period is stated. Repair by substituting "up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Inserted (a) says only "reasonable transition assistance"; no charging basis (then-current rates) appears anywhere in the new operative language.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted (b): "within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control", with the effective date being that of the expiration/termination.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Inserted (b) specifies no format; the agreement's retained Section 9.7 also specifies none. Repair by adding "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification step follows the return; Section 9.7(a) certification applies only to the alternative destruction election, which the new clause expressly overrides ("notwithstanding Section 9.7").

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the 90-day assistance and 30-day return both run from the effective date of any such expiry or termination; the "at AbbVie's request" condition is available after every covered event, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "notwithstanding Section 9.7, within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie" — fixed 30-day deadline anchored to termination/expiry, displacing the request-based, destruction-electable 9.7 mechanic.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).

Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").

Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.

Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".

Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.

No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Inserted (b) specifies no format; the agreement's retained Section 9.7 also specifies none. Repair by adding "in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification step follows the return; Section 9.7(a) certification applies only to the alternative destruction election, which the new clause expressly overrides ("notwithstanding Section 9.7").

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the 90-day assistance and 30-day return both run from the effective date of any such expiry or termination; the "at AbbVie's request" condition is available after every covered event, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination".

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "notwithstanding Section 9.7, within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie" — fixed 30-day deadline anchored to termination/expiry, displacing the request-based, destruction-electable 9.7 mechanic.

payload.feedback:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).
- Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").
- Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.
- Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".
- Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.
- No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent AbbVie Biotechnology Ltd; counterparty is Harpoon Therapeutics, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

input.rationale: Article 12 contains detailed reversion mechanics running to Harpoon (Sections 12.6-12.7), a sell-off right (12.10.2) and survival provisions, but no obligation on Harpoon to support AbbVie's wind-down or to return AbbVie's data on expiry or termination. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, lets Harpoon elect destruction instead of delivery, and sets no deadline ("as soon as reasonably practicable"); Harpoon's other assistance obligations (e.g., Sections 3.12, 4.x) operate during the Term only. The rule therefore fails at the fallback. We insert a new Section 12.11 at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance available on any expiry or termination, and return of AbbVie data within 30 days, expressed as prevailing over the Section 9.7 destruction election so the two mechanics do not conflict. We did not volunteer the preferred six-month period, then-current-rate charging, machine-readable format or deletion certification.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** The agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return obligation running to AbbVie. Article 12's exit mechanics (12.6 reversion, 12.7 Harpoon Reversion Products, 12.10.2 sell-off) all run toward Harpoon, and the only return mechanic — Section 9.7 — is request-based, permits Harpoon to destroy rather than deliver, and has no deadline. Harpoon's assistance obligations elsewhere (Sections 3.12, 4.x, 7.x) are in-Term only.

Classified as **missing** and cured at the **fallback** level with a single inserted Section 12.11: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, plus return of AbbVie data within 30 days, drafted to prevail over the Section 9.7 destruction election so no contradictory mechanic is left behind. Preferred-only extras (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion certification) were deliberately omitted, as were survival and expense tails.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).
- Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").
- Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.
- Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".
- Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.
- No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.

elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (b): "the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (a): "any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The insertion sets the conformance period at "ninety (90) days following delivery", not twelve months; to reach preferred the drafter must change "ninety (90) days" to "twelve (12) months".

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts 90 days.
elements.evidence: The services/Development limb runs only "for thirty (30) days following performance"; preferred requires 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Harpoon shall, at AbbVie's election, repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable, re-perform the non-conforming activities..."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: "...or refund the amounts paid for them", preceded by a narrow override of the non-refundable language in Sections 6.1 through 6.4 so the refund leg is operative.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No warranty of legal compliance was added. Section 3.8.4 is a mutual performance covenant ("shall perform ... in compliance with all Applicable Law") with no warranty framing and no remedy; Sections 10.1/10.2 speak only "as of the Effective Date". Repair requires an express Harpoon warranty of compliance with Applicable Law covering its performance.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code (virus/disabling device) warranty appears anywhere in the retained text or the insertion.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "(a) for ninety (90) days following delivery, any software and other deliverables provided by Harpoon to AbbVie hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation" — exactly the 90-day floor, expressly covering software.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Initial Development Activities and any other Development activities performed by Harpoon hereunder will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — 30-day floor with substantive performance content.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replace the non-conforming deliverable" (plus re-performance for activities).

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: "...or refund the amounts paid for them"; the opening "Notwithstanding any provision of this Agreement stating that payments are non-refundable, including Sections 6.1 through 6.4" prevents the retained non-refundable language from rendering the refund leg inoperative.

elements.element: Warranty survives the disclaimer in Section 10.5.
elements.evidence: Conditional/consequential check: 10.5 already opens "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN", so the new warranty is carved out automatically and no edit to 10.5 was needed — correctly left untouched.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software/deliverable conformance-to-documentation warranty, 30-day professional-and-workmanlike warranty for Harpoon's Development activities, and repair/replace, re-perform and refund remedies all appear in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred is not reached and the comment correctly says so: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty or malicious-code warranty. To move to preferred the drafter must (i) change "ninety (90) days" to "twelve (12) months", (ii) change "thirty (30) days" to "ninety (90) days", (iii) add an express Harpoon warranty that its performance complies with Applicable Law (Section 3.8.4 is a covenant, not a warranty, and carries no remedy), and (iv) add a no-malicious-code warranty.

The insertion is a concise new clause for a missing warranty, so wholly new wording is acceptable; it adds no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no notice procedure and no extra damages categories, and it leaves Sections 10.1, 10.2 and 10.5 untouched.

The narrow non-refundable override is justified by necessity rather than an extra: without it the retained "non-refundable, non-creditable" language in Section 6.1 (and 6.2-6.4) would contradict the refund element, so intent is preserved rather than disturbed. Confirm before sending that Sections 6.2 through 6.4 in fact contain the non-refundable payment mechanics, otherwise narrow the cite to avoid a dangling cross-reference.

Negotiation note (not a defect against the checklist): the remedy is framed "at AbbVie's election" whereas playbook model language puts the choice at Vendor's option; if Harpoon pushes back, conceding "at Harpoon's option" still satisfies every fallback element.

input.summary: Insert Section 12.11 requiring Harpoon, on any expiry or termination, to provide at least 90 days of transition assistance and to return AbbVie's data within 30 days, without disturbing Section 9.7's retention proviso or the Article 12 reversion regime.
input.comment: [Playbook] Article 12 gives Harpoon reversion rights but gives us no exit support, and Section 9.7 only offers a request-based return that Harpoon may satisfy by destruction on no fixed timetable. We added our fallback transition position: at least 90 days of assistance on any expiry or termination and return of our data within 30 days, carved out for data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving reversion provisions.

ops.text: Transition Assistance; Return of AbbVie Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Harpoon shall (a) at AbbVie's request, provide AbbVie with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following the effective date of such expiration or termination, and (b) notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b), within thirty (30) days after such effective date, return to AbbVie all data of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or control, other than data to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent AbbVie Biotechnology Ltd; counterparty is Harpoon Therapeutics, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** The agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return obligation running to AbbVie. Article 12's exit mechanics (12.6 reversion, 12.7 Harpoon Reversion Products, 12.10.2 sell-off) all run toward Harpoon, and the only return mechanic — Section 9.7 — is request-based, permits Harpoon to destroy rather than deliver, and has no deadline. Harpoon's assistance obligations elsewhere (Sections 3.12, 4.x, 7.x) are in-Term only.

Classified as **missing** and cured at the **fallback** level with a single inserted Section 12.11: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, plus return of AbbVie data within 30 days, drafted to prevail over the Section 9.7 destruction election so no contradictory mechanic is left behind. Preferred-only extras (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion certification) were deliberately omitted, as were survival and expense tails.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).
- Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").
- Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.
- Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".
- Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.
- No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.
