system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.

Parties: we represent AbbVie Biotechnology Ltd; counterparty is Harpoon Therapeutics, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

The rule therefore fails at the fallback. We insert a new Section 12.11 at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance available on any expiry or termination, and return of AbbVie data within 30 days, expressed as prevailing over the Section 9.7 destruction election so the two mechanics do not conflict. We did not volunteer the preferred six-month period, then-current-rate charging, machine-readable format or deletion certification.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** The agreement has no post-termination transition or data-return obligation running to AbbVie. Article 12's exit mechanics (12.6 reversion, 12.7 Harpoon Reversion Products, 12.10.2 sell-off) all run toward Harpoon, and the only return mechanic — Section 9.7 — is request-based, permits Harpoon to destroy rather than deliver, and has no deadline. Harpoon's assistance obligations elsewhere (Sections 3.12, 4.x, 7.x) are in-Term only.

Classified as **missing** and cured at the **fallback** level with a single inserted Section 12.11: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, plus return of AbbVie data within 30 days, drafted to prevail over the Section 9.7 destruction election so no contradictory mechanic is left behind. Preferred-only extras (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion certification) were deliberately omitted, as were survival and expense tails.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Position-complete at the fallback: all three fallback elements are met in operative language (any expiry/termination trigger, at least 90 days of assistance, 30-day return anchored to the effective date). Preferred is not reached (90 days rather than six months, no then-current-rate charging, no machine-readable format, no post-return deletion certificate).
- Minimality defect 1 — over-broad override: a blanket "notwithstanding Section 9.7" is wider than the fallback checklist requires. Only the Section 9.7(a) destruction election and the "as soon as reasonably practicable" timing needed to be displaced; as drafted the override also strips Harpoon's retained one-copy proviso for continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival purposes and automatic back-ups. Narrow it to "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)" (or "without limiting Section 9.7").
- Minimality defect 2 — scope beyond the element: limb (b) requires return of "all data and other Confidential Information of AbbVie", extending the obligation past the Customer-Data export element to all AbbVie Confidential Information. Confine limb (b) to AbbVie's data (and Confidential Information constituting AbbVie data) unless a broader return is separately required.
- Intent defect — contradiction with retained termination mechanics: limb (b) requires return of "all data ... of AbbVie in Harpoon's possession or Control" with no carve-out for information Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, so it collides with the Article 12 reversion regime (Sections 12.6-12.7) under which AbbVie data, know-how and regulatory materials pass to and are used by Harpoon post-termination. Repair by adding: "other than data and Confidential Information to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7".
- Drafting check — the inserted clause uses the capitalised term "Control" for physical data holdings; in this agreement "Control" is an IP/licensing concept. Confirm the defined term or replace with lower-case "control" to avoid an unintended or dangling defined-term reference.
- No other retained language was deleted or paraphrased, and Sections 9.7 and 12.10.2 otherwise survive intact; the finding's "missing" classification is sound because no existing provision imposes wind-down assistance or a deadline-bound return on Harpoon.

Re-read any needed source text, validate the revised proposal, rebuild elementCoverage, and submit again.

Resubmitted with the verifier's defects repaired.

**Changes made to the inserted Section 12.11:**
1. **Narrowed the override** — "notwithstanding Section 9.7" became "notwithstanding the destruction election and timing in Section 9.7(a)-(b)", so Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso (continuing obligations, Applicable Law, litigation/archival) and automatic back-up carve-out remain intact.

3. **Removed the contradiction with the reversion regime** — added "other than data to which Harpoon retains rights under the surviving provisions of this Agreement, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7", so the clause no longer collides with the post-termination transfer of data, know-how and regulatory materials to Harpoon.
4. **Defined-term fix** — lower-case "control" replaces the capitalised IP/licensing term "Control".

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

Finding rationale:
Article 12 contains detailed reversion mechanics running to Harpoon (Sections 12.6-12.7), a sell-off right (12.10.2) and survival provisions, but imposes no obligation on Harpoon to support AbbVie's wind-down or to return AbbVie's data on expiry or termination. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, lets Harpoon elect destruction instead of delivery, and sets no deadline ("as soon as reasonably practicable"); Harpoon's other assistance obligations operate during the Term only. The rule therefore fails at the fallback. We insert a new Section 12.11 at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, and return of AbbVie data within 30 days of the effective date. The override is narrowed to the Section 9.7(a)-(b) destruction election and timing so Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso and back-up carve-out survive; limb (b) is confined to AbbVie data (not all AbbVie Confidential Information), uses lower-case "control" to avoid the IP-specific defined term, and carves out data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7, so it does not collide with the reversion regime. We did not volunteer the preferred six-month period, then-current-rate charging, machine-readable format or deletion certification.

Section 7.1.1 gives each Party sole ownership of the Information, inventions and IP it creates and of its background IP, and Section 3.8.2(c) makes AbbVie the sole owner of all Regulatory Documentation (including Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling) for the Licensed Compounds/Products, with Harpoon obliged to execute confirmatory assignments to AbbVie. No AbbVie IP or data is assigned to Harpoon anywhere: Section 5.2 grants Harpoon only a non-exclusive, non-sublicensable licence under AbbVie Patents/Know-How \"solely to the extent necessary for Harpoon to perform its obligations as set forth in, and subject to, the Initial Development Plan,\" and Section 5.6.2 confirms no other AbbVie rights are granted — i.e., Harpoon's licence in our data is confined to service delivery. Harpoon's retention of its own platform know-how (Section 5.6.1) is expressly permitted by the playbook. Joint ownership is created by Section 7.1.2, but it is workable rather than walk-away: each Party may Exploit Joint IP without consent or accounting, and the only overlays (AbbVie's own exclusive licences and Harpoon's exclusivity covenant) run in our favour. On the licence side, Section 5.1.3 gives AbbVie an exclusive licence to Exploit in the Territory (defined at 1.145 as \"the entire world\"), Section 5.3 permits sublicensing through multiple tiers to Affiliates and other Persons, and Section 12.1.2 provides that on expiration the grants become \"non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable.\" Noted but not flagged: the licence is royalty-bearing and revocable during the Term (the core commercial bargain of an option/licence deal, priced under Article 6), and the preferred \"no joint ownership\" position is not achieved. The Section 12.7.1 reversion is a conditional, royalty-bearing licence of a defined AbbVie Reversion IP set — not an assignment of our IP. Several sub-clauses of 7.1.2 and 12.7 are redacted ([***]), so those carve-outs could not be verified.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-8f40b311","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.2.2 In the event of [***]","rationale":"Section 13.4.1 gives us the affiliate and successor carve-out we need, but it is fully mutual: Harpoon may likewise assign to its Affiliate or to a successor without our consent, and nothing bars an assignment to a Competitor. The clause therefore fails the fallback (the retained no-consent affiliate exception means not every non-successor assignment requires consent, and there is no written-notice mechanic) and fails preferred elements 3 and 5. We therefore target the preferred position rather than the fallback, which would require stripping our own affiliate right. The consent standard we need for Harpoon assignments is already in the clause (\"not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed\"), so we leave it verbatim. On change of control, Harpoon's only termination rights are material breach (12.2) and insolvency (12.4) and Section 13.2 addresses only a Change in Control of Harpoon; we add one short confirming sentence so the position is express. Section 13.2's Harpoon-side change of control regime (notice, JGC disbandment, Competing Product provisions) is favourable to us and is untouched.","proposal":"Limit the no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out in Section 13.4.1 to AbbVie, bar assignment by Harpoon to a Competitor, and confirm an AbbVie Change in Control gives Harpoon no termination right.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-bdff7e77","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement (Section 5.8, p0368-p0369) runs against Harpoon, the counterparty: Harpoon and its Affiliates may not develop, commercialize or enable Third Parties to exploit any Competing Product in the Territory, with only an Acquisition/Change in Control carve-out that requires the acquirer to Segregate the Competing Product and preserves AbbVie's unilateral rights to cut off its Confidential Information and disband the JGC. That is exclusivity in our favour and is expressly acceptable under the rule. Searches for sourcing or non-compete duties on AbbVie (\"sole supplier\", requirements purchase, \"AbbVie shall not\", non-compete, supply) return nothing restrictive: to the contrary, AbbVie has the sole right to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply Licensed Compounds and Products (Section 4.5.1, p0340), may appoint distributors and co-promotion partners in its sole discretion (Sections 5.4-5.5, p0360-p0361) and may sublicense through multiple tiers (Section 5.3). The exclusive licences granted to AbbVie at Section 5.1.3 and Harpoon's retained rights at Section 5.6.1 impose no reciprocal sourcing obligation on us. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer); no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-32d8e98d","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee or early-termination-fee payable by AbbVie, so it meets the preferred position. AbbVie's termination for any or no reason on 90 days' notice (Section 12.3) carries no exit payment: the consequences in Section 12.6.1 are limited to cessation of licences and reversion of Licensed Compounds/Products, with no fee. The payment provisions are ordinary consideration (upfront and milestone payments under Sections 6.1-6.3, royalties) rather than penalties; late-payment interest (Section 6.10) and audit cost-shifting on a material variance (Section 6.11) are customary mechanics, not liquidated damages. Article 11 further excludes punitive and consequential damages, and Section 12.9 preserves ordinary law/equity remedies without any stipulated sum. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-87b926c1","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The grant to us (AbbVie as licensee under Sections 5.1.1-5.1.3) meets, and in fact exceeds, the fallback position, so we do not redline it. (i) Affiliates: Section 5.3 lets us sublicense through multiple tiers to \"its Affiliates and other Persons\" with no Harpoon consent (only a post-execution copy), which also captures contractors/third parties acting for us; Sections 5.4, 5.5 and 13.16 reinforce Affiliate rights. This is better than the fallback's \"covered on written notice\". (ii) Successor transfer: Section 13.4.1 permits assignment \"without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates\", satisfying both the fallback M&A transfer and the preferred successor transfer. (iii) Not revocable at will: Harpoon may terminate only for uncured material breach under Section 12.2.1 (90-day cure), the related diligence provision 12.2.2, or insolvency under Section 12.4 — there is no discretionary revocation. (iv) Paid-up position: Section 12.1.2 provides that on expiry of the Term the Section 5.1.3 grants \"shall become non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable\", delivering the preferred perpetual/irrevocable paid-up outcome. Minor points short of the ideal preferred wording — the insolvency termination trigger in Section 12.4, and the fact that post-expiry irrevocability converts the grant to non-exclusive and attaches only to the Section 5.1.3 licences — are noted but are customary in this deal structure and are not material fallback failures.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-6fa71867","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11 INDEMNITY","rationale":"Section 11.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision: a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages with carve-outs, but with no monetary cap. Searches for aggregate liability, shall not exceed, and in no event surface no cap anywhere in the Agreement; the only limits are the insurance minima in Section 11.6. Both Parties' direct liability is therefore unlimited, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term (no mutual cap based on 12 months of fees). We target the fallback: one inserted sentence adds a mutual cap at twelve months' fees with indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap. We did not add the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, data-protection or IP-infringement carve-outs, or the payment-obligations exclusion, as those sit above the fallback threshold; fraud already sits outside the 11.5 waiver.","proposal":"Insert a mutual aggregate liability cap of 12 months' fees after Section 11.5, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-f38ffb5e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 GRANT OF RIGHTS","rationale":"The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement (Section 5.8) binds Harpoon and its Affiliates, not AbbVie; Section 5.6.1 confirms Harpoon's retained rights are \"subject to Section 5.8\", and Section 7.2 refers to \"in the case of Harpoon, its exclusivity obligations hereunder\". That restriction runs in our favour and is not flagged. Searches for reciprocal covenants (\"AbbVie shall not\", \"AbbVie may not\", \"neither Party shall\", \"directly or indirectly\", \"Competing Product\") return no non-compete, field-of-use or territory covenant binding AbbVie: Article 4 gives AbbVie sole Commercialization rights, Section 10.4 (Covenants of AbbVie) contains only an IP-assignment covenant, and Article 12 imposes no post-termination competition restraint. The licence scope in Section 5.1.3 (Field/Territory) is a grant boundary, not a covenant restricting our business. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-906bc2a0","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 12.3 gives us (AbbVie) an unconditional right to terminate for any or no reason — in entirety or country-by-country — on ninety (90) days' prior written notice, which sits squarely within the fallback range of 60–90 days' notice. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches: the consequences in Sections 12.6.1, 12.8 and 12.10 are reversion/wind-down and accrued-payment provisions only (the upfront and milestone amounts in Article 6 are non-refundable payments already earned, not a termination charge), so the three-months-of-fees cap is satisfied a fortiori. Harpoon's termination rights are confined to material breach (12.2.1, 12.2.2) and insolvency (12.4); it has no convenience right at all, which exceeds both the fallback (end-of-term only, 90 days' notice) and the preferred element that Vendor have no convenience right during a committed term. The bargain therefore meets every fallback element on its material terms and we do not redline it. Short of preferred only on notice length (90 rather than 30 days) and the absence of a prepaid-fee pro-rata refund mechanic, which is immaterial in this milestone/royalty structure — noted, not flagged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-79377fe7","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 6.5.3 Reductions. Notwithstanding the foregoing:","rationale":"Section 6.11 is the only audit right binding us (the Section 3.8.5/3.8.6 inspection rights run in our favour and are not flagged). It uses an independent nationally recognised accounting firm reasonably acceptable to us and is confined to books and records (no systems access), and Section 6.13 imposes confidentiality on the review, so the qualitative protections are sound. However, the three fallback numeric terms are all left open: the audit frequency period, any prior-notice requirement, and the variance threshold that shifts cost to us (\"unless the audit reveals a variance [***] from the reported amounts\") are unspecified, so on its face the clause permits repeated, unannounced audits and cost-shifting on any variance. We therefore fix them at the fallback level (once per twelve-month period, fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, cost on Harpoon unless underpayment exceeds 10%). We note but have not redlined Section 6.12, which lets the Audit Expert allocate initial audit costs in a disputed audit.","proposal":"Fix audit frequency, notice and cost-shift threshold in Section 6.11 at the fallback position.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-ccc10a09","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.4.2 [***]","rationale":"Governing law is Delaware (Section 13.6.1), which sits at our fallback. However, the Agreement designates no court forum at all: Section 13.6 is captioned \\\"Jurisdiction\\\" but contains only a service provision referring to \\\"any such court,\\\" and Section 13.7.1 lets either Party elect binding arbitration under Schedule 13.7.3, whose seat and rules are redacted. The fallback requires the corresponding Delaware courts as the dispute forum, so the forum element fails materially. Our single edit routes unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, leaving the Delaware governing law, the Senior Officer step, the IP carve-out in 13.7.2 and the interim-relief carve-out in 13.7.5 untouched.","proposal":"Replace the party-elected arbitration route with exclusive litigation in the Delaware state and federal courts, matching the Delaware governing law already selected.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-25f546cc","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11 INDEMNITY","rationale":"Article 11's architecture already meets the structural preferred elements in our favour: Harpoon expressly indemnifies and defends AbbVie and its Affiliates against Third Party Claims (11.2), with prompt written notice (11.3), allocation of control of the defence (11.4.1, with AbbVie controlling where Harpoon does not assume) and reasonable cooperation (11.4.4). What fails is scope: the trigger lists of both 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted, so no operative text evidences that Harpoon's indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement, Harpoon's breach of Applicable Law, a Harpoon-caused data breach, or Harpoon's gross negligence/willful misconduct, and nothing confines our own 11.1 indemnity to AbbVie-provided content and AbbVie's breach of law. Section 7.4's \"Subject to Section 11.2\" cross-reference is inference only and cannot substitute for a trigger. We therefore add the four Harpoon-side triggers as an additive \"without limiting the foregoing\" list inside 11.2 (so any equivalent redacted trigger is preserved rather than duplicated or overwritten) and add one sentence limiting 11.1. We do not add the fallback's 3x-annual-fees super-cap: Harpoon's indemnity is currently uncapped (11.5 restricts only consequential damages), which is better for us.","proposal":"Add the four Harpoon-side indemnity triggers to Section 11.2 and cap the scope of AbbVie's indemnity in Section 11.1.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mfn-79632a9a","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.4.2 [***]","rationale":"Targeted searches across the Agreement (most favored/favoured nation, \"no less favorable\", \"at least as favorable\", best price, right to match, first negotiation/refusal, comparable third-party terms) return no MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction. Nothing obliges AbbVie (Customer) to extend to Harpoon (Vendor) terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, or to match a third-party offer, and the integration clause confirms the Agreement and its Schedules are the complete bargain. The rule's preferred position — no MFN obligation burdening Customer — is therefore met on the face of the document, so no redline is warranted. Note only that portions of the Agreement are redacted ([***]), so this conclusion rests on the visible text.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-66bb9961","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 COMMERCIALIZATION","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, volume, requirements or take-or-pay obligation on AbbVie, so it sits at the preferred position. Searches for \"minimum\", take-or-pay, shortfall, purchase/volume commitment, forecast and requirements/sole-source language returned nothing responsive: the only \"minimum\" hits are the insurance limits in Sections 11.6-11.6.1 (p0573-p0577), which are unrelated. AbbVie's payment obligations are event-contingent consideration for the rights granted - a one-time upfront payment (Section 6.1), development and regulatory milestones payable only on achievement of the specified milestone (Section 6.2), and royalties on actual Net Sales - none of which require AbbVie to buy any quantity or to pay for unused volume. On supply, Section 4.5.1 gives AbbVie the sole right to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply Licensed Compounds and Products at its own expense, and Section 4.5.2 entitles AbbVie to a manufacturing technology transfer, so there is no obligation to source from Harpoon. Article 4.2's Commercially Reasonable Efforts commercialization diligence is a separate efforts standard, not a volume or purchase commitment, and is not flagged here. No redline is warranted; the fallback true-up/reduction mechanics are unnecessary because no commitment exists to reduce.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-401bc47e","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 10.4 Covenants of AbbVie. AbbVie covenants to Harpoon as follows:","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"solicitation\", \"recruit\", \"induce\", \"no-hire\", \"employ or engage\", \"non-compete\" and restrictive-covenant language return no responsive provisions anywhere in the Agreement. The only personnel-related terms are confidentiality/assignment-of-inventions covenants (e.g., AbbVie's sole covenant at 10.4.1 and Harpoon's mirror at 10.3.4), debarment representations, and meeting/attendance provisions — none of which restrict either Party from soliciting, hiring, or employing the other's personnel. AbbVie is therefore subject to no non-solicitation or no-hire restriction, which satisfies the preferred position (\"No non-solicit on Customer\"). No redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-9ed7d242","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement has no automatic-renewal mechanic. Section 12.1.1 sets a single Term running from the Effective Date until expiry of the last Royalty Term (or lapse of the License Option), and searches for \"renew\", \"renewal term\", \"extension of the Term\", price-uplift and CPI language return nothing in the operative terms. There is therefore no evergreen roll-over, no non-renewal notice window to compute, and no renewal price-increase right, so the conditional fallback elements (60-day non-renewal window; 5% uplift cap) and the conditional preferred elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) are inapplicable rather than unmet. Any extension of the Term would require a mutual written amendment: \"No amendment, modification, release, or discharge with respect to this Agreement shall be binding upon the Parties unless in writing and duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties\" (Section 13.9), which satisfies the preferred position's mutual-written-agreement baseline. Section 12.1.2 further improves our position on expiry by converting the Section 5.1.3 grants to non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable. Nothing here requires a redline; the clause sits at or above the preferred position.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-19e54735","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 10 REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES","rationale":"Article 10 contains only mutual and Harpoon-specific representations given \"as of the Effective Date\" (10.1, 10.2) plus covenants (10.3, 10.4). The closest performance standard, Section 3.8.4 (\"in good scientific manner and in compliance with all Applicable Law\"), is a mutual compliance covenant, not a conformance warranty, and carries no remedy. Nothing warrants that Harpoon's deliverables or any software conform to their documentation, and no repair, replacement or refund remedy exists (searches for \"conform\", \"re-perform\" and \"refund\" return only tax and indemnity mechanics). The disclaimer at 10.5 preserves \"THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH HEREIN\", so it needs no carve-out edit — but there is nothing for it to preserve. This fails the fallback on material terms, so we inserted the shortest express warranty at fallback level: 90 days for software/deliverables, 30 days for Harpoon's Development activities, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund. Because Sections 6.1 through 6.4 make payments \"non-refundable\", the remedy sentence opens with a narrow override so the refund leg is not read as inoperative; the services leg also reaches Harpoon's other Development activities so the warranty is not under-inclusive. We did not take the preferred 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code elements.","proposal":"Insert Section 10.6 express performance warranty: 90-day conformance for software/deliverables, 30-day warranty for Harpoon's Development activities, with repair/replacement, re-performance or refund, and a targeted override of the non-refundable payment language in Sections 6.1-6.4.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-45fedb34","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 11 INDEMNITY","rationale":"Section 11.6 has a real mutual insurance framework (workers' compensation at statutory limits, employer's liability, general liability including clinical trial cover, certificates on request, and an AbbVie self-insurance right at 11.6.3), but the schedule of coverages in 11.6.1 contains no professional liability (errors and omissions) and no cyber/privacy liability coverage anywhere in the document. That fails the fallback position (E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M), so we insert the two missing coverages only. We target the fallback rather than preferred limits because the general liability limits are redacted and the fallback is the shortest complete cure; the coverage is drafted as a Harpoon obligation so as not to add a new mutual burden on AbbVie.","proposal":"Add Harpoon-only E&O USD 1M and cyber/privacy USD 2M coverage to the Section 11.6.1 schedule of minimum limits.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-10013887","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 9 CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE","rationale":"Article 12 contains detailed reversion mechanics running to Harpoon (Sections 12.6-12.7), a sell-off right (12.10.2) and survival provisions, but imposes no obligation on Harpoon to support AbbVie's wind-down or to return AbbVie's data on expiry or termination. The only return mechanic is Section 9.7, which is request-based, lets Harpoon elect destruction instead of delivery, and sets no deadline (\"as soon as reasonably practicable\"); Harpoon's other assistance obligations operate during the Term only. The rule therefore fails at the fallback. We insert a new Section 12.11 at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance available after any expiry or termination, and return of AbbVie data within 30 days of the effective date. The override is narrowed to the Section 9.7(a)-(b) destruction election and timing so Harpoon's one-copy retention proviso and back-up carve-out survive; limb (b) is confined to AbbVie data (not all AbbVie Confidential Information), uses lower-case \"control\" to avoid the IP-specific defined term, and carves out data Harpoon retains rights to under the surviving provisions, including Sections 12.6 and 12.7, so it does not collide with the reversion regime. We did not volunteer the preferred six-month period, then-current-rate charging, machine-readable format or deletion certification.","proposal":"Insert Section 12.11 requiring Harpoon, on any expiry or termination, to provide at least 90 days of transition assistance and to return AbbVie's data within 30 days, without disturbing Section 9.7's retention proviso or the Article 12 reversion regime.","verification":"repaired"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Development and Option Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Development and Option Agreement (AbbVie as Customer/licensee; Harpoon as counterparty)

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Development and Option Agreement against the playbook. On balance the Agreement is strongly favourable to us on the core commercial architecture: the licence grant to us exceeds the fallback (worldwide exclusive licence, multi-tier sublicensing without consent, and conversion to a non-exclusive, fully-paid, royalty-free and irrevocable grant on expiry under Section 12.1.2); we hold an unconditional 90-day termination-for-convenience right (Section 12.3) with no exit fee; and the only exclusivity/non-compete covenant in the document (Section 5.8) binds Harpoon, not us. There are no minimum purchase commitments, no MFN mechanic, no non-solicitation restriction on us, no liquidated damages payable by us, and no auto-renewal.

Seven items require attention. Two are high severity: (i) the assignment clause (Section 13.4.1) is fully mutual, letting Harpoon assign to an Affiliate or successor without our consent and with no bar on assignment to a Competitor; and (ii) Section 11.5 waives indirect and consequential damages but contains no monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement, leaving direct liability unlimited on both sides. Four medium items concern the open numeric terms in the audit clause (Section 6.11), the absence of any designated court forum notwithstanding the Delaware governing law (Section 13.6), the redacted indemnity triggers in Article 11, and the absence of any performance warranty in Article 10. Two low-severity gaps are missing E&O and cyber insurance in the Section 11.6.1 schedule, and the absence of post-termination transition assistance and data-return obligations on Harpoon.

We note that several provisions are redacted ([***]) — including sub-clauses of Sections 7.1.2 and 12.7, the Article 11 indemnity trigger lists, the general liability limits in Section 11.6.1, the audit variance threshold in Section 6.11, and the arbitration seat and rules in Schedule 13.7.3 — so certain conclusions rest on the visible text only.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 7 Intellectual Property | Sits at or above fallback; no AbbVie IP or data assigned to Harpoon. Joint ownership under 7.1.2 is workable (each Party may Exploit without consent or accounting). Some 7.1.2/12.7 carve-outs redacted. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 13.4.1 / § 13.2 | Mutual no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out and no bar on assignment to a Competitor; fails fallback. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 11.5 | Mutual consequential-damages waiver but no monetary cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 5 (5.8) | Only exclusivity covenant runs against Harpoon; no sourcing or non-compete duty on us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 | No LDs, penalties, minimum fees or early-termination fees payable by us. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 5 (5.1.1–5.1.3, 5.3) | Exceeds fallback; paid-up irrevocable grant on expiry (§ 12.1.2). Insolvency trigger (§ 12.4) noted only. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 5 | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory covenant binding us. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12.3 | Unconditional 90-day right, no fee; Harpoon has no convenience right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 6.11 | Frequency, notice and variance threshold all left open ([***]); permits repeated unannounced audits. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 13.6 / § 13.7 | Delaware law (fallback) but no court forum designated; either Party may elect arbitration under a redacted schedule. |
| Medium | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 11.1–11.2 | Structure meets preferred, but trigger lists are redacted; no verifiable IP, law, data-breach or GN/WM trigger. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | **Deviation** | § 10 | Article 10 contains only Effective-Date reps and covenants; no conformance warranty and no remedy. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 13 | No MFN, best-price or right-to-match mechanic in either direction. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4 (4.5.1–4.5.2) | No minimum, volume or take-or-pay obligation; we hold sole Manufacture/supply rights. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 10.4 | No solicitation, recruitment or no-hire restriction on us. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12.1 | No evergreen mechanic; extension requires mutual written amendment (§ 13.9). |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 11.6.1 | No professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy coverage in the schedule. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | § 9.7 / Art. 12 | No wind-down support obligation; § 9.7 return is request-based, allows destruction election, no deadline. |

---

## 3. Proposed redlines (deviations and gaps)

1. **Assignment (§ 13.4.1)** — Limit the no-consent affiliate/successor carve-out to AbbVie, bar assignment by Harpoon to a Competitor, and add one sentence confirming that an AbbVie Change in Control gives Harpoon no termination right. We leave the existing "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" consent standard verbatim, and leave Section 13.2's Harpoon-side Change in Control regime (which is favourable to us) untouched.
2. **Liability cap (after § 11.5)** — Insert a mutual aggregate cap at twelve months' fees, with indemnification, Article 9 confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly uncapped. We are targeting the fallback only; we have not sought the USD 1,000,000 floor or the additional preferred carve-outs.
3. **Audit (§ 6.11)** — Fix the open terms at fallback: once per twelve-month period, fifteen (15) days' prior written notice, and cost on Harpoon unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
